title: Ramanujam--Samuel parafactorial localizations of a formally smooth local algebra
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, and let $\rho:A\to B$ be a local homomorphism (so $\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$). Suppose the $\mathfrak m_A$-adic completion $\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], $\dim B>\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $B/\mathfrak m_B$ is a finite extension of $A/\mathfrak m_A$. Suppose $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_AB$ is prime. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ not contained in $\mathfrak p$ with $\dim B_{\mathfrak q}\ge2$, put $R=B_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $P=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak qR\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion]. The restriction $R\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ is an isomorphism, and every invertible $\mathcal O_P$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_P$.

source.place: EGA IV4 Theorem 21.14.1 and Corollary 21.14.2, with the explicit meaning of local parafactoriality in 21.13.8. No Stacks tag states this Ramanujam--Samuel theorem. Read in the online English EGA translation; local EGA IV4 WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-formally-smooth-normal-power-series-cover] to the given local map. Its hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses on $A,B,\mathfrak p$ in the statement. Obtain $B\to D=C[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$, faithfully flat and local, with $C,D$ Noetherian normal local domains and inverse image of $\mathfrak nD$ equal to $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-normal-ring-descent], $B$ is normal. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with the zero ideal, $B\to D$ is injective, so $B$ is a domain as well.

source.place: EGA IV4 proof of 21.14.1, first paragraph: the power-series cover and normality descent. EGA IV4 is WANTED locally; read the online English translation.

proof.text: Fix a height-one prime $\mathfrak r$ of $B$ with $\mathfrak r\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. It is a nonzero reflexive ideal: [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices] gives the reflexive lattice $I_B([\mathfrak r])$, which equals $\mathfrak r$. Indeed its elements lie in $B$ by the height-one intersection formula, and its one positive valuation condition says membership in $\mathfrak rB_{\mathfrak r}\cap B=\mathfrak r$; conversely every element of $\mathfrak r$ satisfies those inequalities. Choose $c\in\mathfrak r\setminus\mathfrak p$. Its image is outside $\mathfrak nD$. Thus every height-one prime of $D$ containing $\mathfrak rD$ contains that image and is not contained in $\mathfrak nD$. Each is principal by [lem-sfb-complete-normal-horizontal-primes-principal]. Now [lem-sfb-reflexive-ideal-principal-flat-descent], with $I=\mathfrak r$, proves $\mathfrak r=(h_{\mathfrak r})$ in $B$. Both rings are normal Noetherian local domains by step 1, so all descent hypotheses hold.

source.place: EGA IV4 proof of 21.14.1, reduction to the power-series case and the subsequent horizontal-prime calculation. EGA IV4 is WANTED locally; read the online English translation.

proof.text: Verify the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-principal-divisor-punctured-local-criterion]. Let $D_0=(d_{\mathfrak r})$ be a finite Weil divisor and $a\in\operatorname{Frac}(B)^\times$ with $d_{\mathfrak r}=v_{\mathfrak r}(a)$ for all height-one $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$. By [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel], $E=D_0-\operatorname{div}_B(a)$ has finite support, and its coefficients on these primes are zero. For each prime in the remaining support, step 2 gives $\mathfrak r=(h_{\mathfrak r})$. At $\mathfrak r$, $h_{\mathfrak r}$ generates the maximal ideal of the DVR $B_{\mathfrak r}$, hence has valuation one. At any different height-one prime $\mathfrak s$, it is a unit, since $h_{\mathfrak r}\in\mathfrak s$ would imply $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak s$ and thus equality. Therefore $b=a\prod_{\mathfrak r\in\operatorname{supp}E}h_{\mathfrak r}^{e_{\mathfrak r}}$ has valuation $d_{\mathfrak s}$ at every height-one prime. Negative exponents are taken in the fraction field, and the empty product is one. The valuation homomorphism in the cited node proves this coefficient by coefficient.

source.place: EGA IV4 21.14.1, reduction of the cycle assertion to principal height-one primes; explicit finite product assembly. EGA IV4 is WANTED locally; read the online English translation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-principal-divisor-punctured-local-criterion] with this $B$ and $\mathfrak p$. Step 1 supplies a Noetherian normal domain, and step 3 supplies its divisor hypothesis. The given $\mathfrak q\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $\dim B_{\mathfrak q}\ge2$ are precisely the remaining hypotheses. Its two conclusions are the asserted restriction isomorphism and triviality of every invertible module on $P$.

source.place: EGA IV4 Corollary 21.14.2: apply 21.13.15 to X=Spec(B), S={p}, then 21.13.8. EGA IV4 is WANTED locally; read the online English translation.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement. Split the EGA proof through a normal power-series cover, horizontal height-one prime principality, generic reflexive-ideal flat descent and the converse divisor criterion. Reused normality descent and the existing divisorial-lattice and principal-divisor theorems. All four new nodes are statement-only and searched.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q87-84f84922c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all four new nodes and every cited statement in full. EGA IV4 is not local, so I read the translation's markdown source (jcreinhold/ega iv/34-ch4-21-divisors.md): 21.13.8, 21.13.14-16, 21.14.1 with its full proof, and 21.14.2. The item statement agrees with 21.14.1/21.14.2 hypothesis by hypothesis; 'p prime' is redundant (EGA step 0) and harmless. Step 1 is EGA's first paragraph (C finite flat over Â, D0=C[[T]]); the contraction holds because n=m_A C, normality descends by 2.1.13, injectivity comes from faithfully flat contraction. Step 2 is EGA's divisorial descent: I_B([r])=r is reflexive by the lattice node, and c in r minus p lies outside nD, so every height-one prime over rD is horizontal and principal. Step 3 is the valuation assembly that proves the conclusion of 21.14.1. Step 4 is 21.13.15 (a)=>(b) with S={p}. 21.13.15(a) is 'cycles on X principal at S are locally principal', so the node's global hypothesis implies it, and EGA's neighbourhood/21.13.14 argument settles points q with p outside Spec B_q. Small cases checked for each new node: the horizontal node's r not-in nD form is the true one (Danilov elliptic-cone examples rule out an 'every class' version), d=0 is vacuous; for the descent node, I=R is allowed and reflexivity is required (an m-primary ideal of a 2-dimensional regular local ring is a counterexample without it); the cover node holds for an inseparable residue extension; the criterion holds for p=(0) (B factorial) and p=m. No duplicates: parafactorial-principal-cycle-extension is the converse direction, punctured-picard-local-extension-criterion is a different statement. No new node restates the item; each is one paragraph of EGA's proof. Tool uses accepted: divisorial-fractional-module-lattices and normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel are generic normal-domain algebra. Batch-5 flags: both trf citations and the lattice node's closure are generic facts about div on Noetherian normal domains (finite support, homomorphism, kernel), and def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group is a general definition; none is a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all are accepted. No SGA source is used. No changes made.
